title: Momentum Module 6 Lesson 1: Multi Collision Chains custom practice

evidence_basis.originality_note: All prompts, numerical values and physical configurations are original; mapped Cambridge past-paper evidence informs cognitive demand and assessment structure only.

parts.prompt: Three particles $A$, $B$, and $C$ of masses $0.2\text{ kg}$, $0.3\text{ kg}$, and $0.5\text{ kg}$ lie at rest in a straight line on a smooth horizontal floor, with $B$ between $A$ and $C$. Particle $A$ is projected towards $B$ with speed $5\text{ m s}^{-1}$. After colliding with $B$, particle $A$ is brought to rest and $B$ moves towards $C$ with speed $v_B$. Particle $B$ then collides with and coalesces with $C$. Calculate the final speed of the combined particle $BC$.

Particles $P$ and $Q$ of masses $0.4\text{ kg}$ and $0.2\text{ kg}$ move towards each other on a smooth line with speeds $3\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and $1\text{ m s}^{-1}$ respectively. After colliding, $P$ continues in its original direction with speed $1\text{ m s}^{-1}$. A third particle $R$ of mass $0.3\text{ kg}$ is initially at rest ahead of $Q$. Find the speed of $Q$ after colliding with $P$, and state whether $Q$ will collide with $R$.

After a series of collisions on a smooth straight line, particles $A$, $B$, and $C$ lie in that order from left to right. Particle $A$ moves to the right with speed $v_A$, particle $B$ moves to the right with speed $4\text{ m s}^{-1}$, and particle $C$ moves to the right with speed $6\text{ m s}^{-1}$. State the condition on $v_A$ such that particle $A$ never collides with $B$ again, and confirm whether $B$ can collide with $C$.

A particle $B$ of mass $0.5\text{ kg}$ is moving towards a smooth vertical wall at $4\text{ m s}^{-1}$. It strikes the wall perpendicularly and rebounds with speed $4\text{ m s}^{-1}$ along the same line. A particle $A$ of mass $0.5\text{ kg}$ is moving towards the wall at $2\text{ m s}^{-1}$ behind $B$. Find the speed of each particle if they coalesce upon colliding with each other after $B$ rebounds from the wall.

A particle $A$ of mass $1\text{ kg}$ moving at $6\text{ m s}^{-1}$ collides with stationary particle $B$ of mass $1\text{ kg}$ and coalesces to form $AB$. The combined body $AB$ then collides with stationary particle $C$ of mass $2\text{ kg}$ and coalesces to form $ABC$. Calculate the total kinetic energy lost over the two collisions.

Particle $B$ is initially at rest at a distance of $6\text{ m}$ from a vertical wall. Particle $A$ collides with $B$, causing $B$ to move directly towards the wall with constant speed $3\text{ m s}^{-1}$. Particle $B$ bounces elastically off the wall (speed unchanged at $3\text{ m s}^{-1}$) and moves back along the same path. Particle $A$ moves towards the wall with constant speed $1\text{ m s}^{-1}$. Calculate the time from the first collision until $A$ and $B$ collide for the second time.

questions.prompt: Three smooth spheres $A$, $B$, and $C$, of masses $0.4\text{ kg}$, $0.6\text{ kg}$, and $0.8\text{ kg}$ respectively, lie in that order in a straight line on a smooth horizontal table. Spheres $B$ and $C$ are initially at rest. Sphere $A$ is projected directly towards $B$ with speed $5\text{ m s}^{-1}$. When $A$ collides with $B$, sphere $A$ continues to move in its original direction with speed $0.5\text{ m s}^{-1}$. Sphere $B$ subsequently collides with and coalesces with sphere $C$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the speed of sphere $B$ immediately after its collision with sphere $A$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Find the common speed of $B$ and $C$ after they coalesce, and explain why there are no further collisions.

questions.prompt: A particle $B$ of mass $0.3\text{ kg}$ is stationary on a smooth horizontal surface at a distance from a vertical wall. Particle $A$ of mass $0.3\text{ kg}$ moves towards $B$ with speed $4\text{ m s}^{-1}$ in a direction perpendicular to the wall. In the first collision between $A$ and $B$, particle $A$ is brought to rest and $B$ moves directly towards the wall. Particle $B$ hits the wall and rebounds elastically (reversing its velocity with unchanged speed), then moves directly back towards $A$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the speed of $B$ after the first collision, and state its speed and direction after rebounding from the wall.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: When $B$ collides with stationary particle $A$ for the second time, they coalesce. Find the final speed and direction of the combined particle.

questions.prompt: Three smooth particles $A$, $B$, and $C$, of masses $0.2\text{ kg}$, $0.3\text{ kg}$, and $0.5\text{ kg}$ respectively, lie in that order in a straight line on a smooth horizontal floor. Particles $B$ and $C$ are initially stationary. Particle $A$ is projected towards $B$ with speed $6\text{ m s}^{-1}$. After $A$ collides with $B$, the speed of $A$ is $1.5\text{ m s}^{-1}$ in its original direction. Particle $B$ then moves on to collide with particle $C$. In this second collision, $B$ and $C$ coalesce.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the speed of $B$ after the first collision, and the common speed of $B$ and $C$ after the second collision.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Show that particle $A$ collides with the combined particle $BC$ in a subsequent impact, and calculate the time taken from the second collision until $A$ collides with $BC$, given that the distance between $B$ and $C$ before their collision was $1.5\text{ m}$.

questions.prompt: A particle $B$ of mass $0.4\text{ kg}$ is initially at rest on a smooth horizontal table at a distance of $2.4\text{ m}$ from a smooth vertical barrier. A particle $A$ of mass $0.2\text{ kg}$ moving at $6\text{ m s}^{-1}$ perpendicularly towards the barrier collides directly with $B$. In this collision, particle $A$ is brought to rest and $B$ moves towards the barrier. Particle $B$ hits the barrier and rebounds with half of its speed before the barrier impact.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the speed of $B$ towards the barrier after the first collision, and the speed of $B$ after it rebounds from the barrier.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Find the total time from the first collision until $B$ collides with $A$ for the second time, given that $A$ remained at rest at the position of the first collision.

questions.prompt: Three particles $P$, $Q$, and $R$ have masses $0.5\text{ kg}$, $0.3\text{ kg}$, and $0.2\text{ kg}$ respectively, and lie in that order in a straight line on a smooth horizontal table. Particles $Q$ and $R$ are at rest. Particle $P$ is projected towards $Q$ with speed $4\text{ m s}^{-1}$. When $P$ collides with $Q$, they coalesce to form a combined particle $S$. Particle $S$ then moves along the line and collides with $R$, coalescing with $R$ to form a final combined particle $T$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the speed of $S$ after the first collision, and the speed of $T$ after the second collision.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Calculate the kinetic energy lost in the first collision, and the additional kinetic energy lost in the second collision.

questions.prompt: A particle $B$ of mass $0.6\text{ kg}$ is initially at rest on a smooth horizontal table at a distance of $3.6\text{ m}$ from a smooth vertical barrier. A particle $A$ of mass $0.3\text{ kg}$ moves towards $B$ at $9\text{ m s}^{-1}$ along the perpendicular line towards the barrier. When $A$ collides with $B$, particle $A$ continues to move towards the barrier with speed $1\text{ m s}^{-1}$, while particle $B$ moves towards the barrier with speed $v_B$. Particle $B$ reaches the barrier and rebounds elastically (its speed is unchanged, and its direction is reversed). Particle $B$ then moves directly towards $A$ and collides with $A$ for a second time.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the speed $v_B$ of particle $B$ immediately after the first collision, and show that particle $B$ takes $0.9\text{ s}$ to reach the barrier from the point of the first collision.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Find the distance of particle $A$ from the barrier at the moment particle $B$ rebounds from the barrier.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Find the total time elapsed from the first collision until $A$ and $B$ collide for the second time.

questions.prompt: Three smooth particles $A$, $B$, and $C$, of masses $m\text{ kg}$, $2\text{ kg}$, and $3\text{ kg}$ respectively, lie in that order in a straight line on a smooth horizontal floor. Particles $B$ and $C$ are initially stationary. Particle $A$ is projected towards $B$ with speed $6\text{ m s}^{-1}$. When $A$ collides with $B$, particle $A$ is brought to rest and $B$ moves with speed $v_B$. Particle $B$ then collides with particle $C$. In this second collision, $B$ rebounds with speed $0.5\text{ m s}^{-1}$ in the direction back towards $A$, and $C$ moves forward with speed $v_C$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Show that the value of $m$ is $1.0\text{ kg}$, find the speed $v_B$ of $B$ after the first collision, and find the speed $v_C$ of $C$ after the second collision.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Particle $B$ moves back towards stationary particle $A$ and collides with $A$ for a second time, coalescing with $A$ to form a combined particle $AB$. Find the speed of $AB$ and verify that $AB$ will never collide with particle $C$.
